## Background

I trained as a mathematician with a focus on **statistical mechanics** — the part
of physics where probability, large systems, and emergent structure meet. Along
the way I picked up a working obsession with **information theory** and its
surprisingly deep ties to **investing and decision-making under uncertainty**.

Most recently I spent several years as a data scientist at an NGO, building
models and pipelines for real-world impact. I've since left to focus on moving
into **quantitative finance** or **AI**, where I can put the mathematical and
computational side of my background to fuller use.

## Research & writing interests

- **Quantitative finance** — modern portfolio theory, log-optimal / Kelly
  investing, risk and drawdown, market microstructure.
- **Information theory** — entropy, the duality between gambling and coding,
  and information geometry.
- **Statistical mechanics & computational physics** — Monte Carlo methods,
  phase transitions, and the math of large interacting systems.
- **Bayesian statistics** — inference, hierarchical models, and the principled
  handling of uncertainty.

## Toolkit

I write a lot of **Python** (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, the usual scientific stack)
and I'm comfortable taking a problem from a whiteboard derivation in **LaTeX**
all the way to a reproducible, tested implementation.

Roles in **quantitative investing** or **applied AI / research** where rigorous
